question: Alicia had two containers. The first was \(\frac{5}{6}\) full of water and the second was empty. She poured all the water from the first container into the second container, at which point the second container was \(\frac{3}{4}\) full of water. What is the ratio of the volume of the smaller container to the volume of the larger container?
solution:
The amount of water stays the same when Alicia pours it into the second container. Let \(x\) and \(y\) be the full capacities of the first and second containers, respectively. Then
\[
\frac56x=\frac34y.
\]
Dividing by \(y\) and then by \(\frac56\) gives
\[
\frac{x}{y}=\frac34\div\frac56
=\frac34\cdot\frac65
=\frac9{10}.
\]
Since this ratio is less than \(1\), the first container is smaller. The requested ratio is therefore \(\boxed{\frac9{10}}\), choice \(\text{(D)}\).
